ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended through Act No. 20200; Enforcement Decree No. 33569), commonly cited as the Financial Information Act; Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality Act (Act No. 6815, as amended); Commercial Act (Act No. 8429) for corporate registry and share register obligations; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 14268) for cross-border capital remittance; Financial Services Commission and Financial Intelligence Unit of Korea enforcement rules and AML/CFT guidelines implementing FATF Recommendations 24 and 25.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Parent Company / Ultimate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry / Registrar of Companies of the parent entity's jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, Hong Kong Companies Registry, or domestic Secretary of State business registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille state): notarize the certificate watermarked copy, obtain an Apostille from the competent authority (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs or State Department/Secretary of State), commission a certified Korean translation, then submit to the Korean registry. Do NOT add consular legalization. Path B (non-Apostille state): notarize, authenticate at the parent country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalize at the Korean Embassy/Consulate in the parent country, then commission a certified Korean translation. Paths A and B are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille with Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence (Statutory or Annual Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Companies or tax authority in the parent company's jurisdiction as evidenced by a current certificate which must remain valid as at the application date
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille state): notarize, apostille from the competent state authority, translate into Korean by a certified translator. Path B (non-Apostille state): notarize, foreign-ministry authentication, Korean consular legalization, and certified Korean translation. Apostille and consular legalization must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney Appointing the Korean Sub-Agent and Authorizing the Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered director of the parent entity, authenticated according to corporate governance rules
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille state): notarize the chairperson's or corporate secretary's signature, apostille via the competent authority, and produce a certified Korean translation. Path B (non-Apostille state): notarize, authenticate at the foreign ministry, legalize at the Korean Embassy/Consulate, and produce a certified Korean translation. Both paths are self-contained; approval under one path excludes the other.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Parent Entity (Memorandum and Articles or Charter and By-Laws)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent company's registered office and authenticated by the competent registration authority or corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille state): notarize the copy or extract, issue an Apostille from the designated ministry, then have a certified Korean translation prepared. Path B (non-Apostille state): notarize, authenticate at the foreign ministry, legalize at the Korean consulate, then prepare a certified Korean translation. No mixture of legalization regimes is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate Bank Reference Letter (issued by the Parent Company's Principal Bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank branch treasury / trade finance department where the parent maintains its operational current account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille state): banker's official signature notarized, Apostille obtained from the central or competent issuing authority, and certified Korean translation attached. Path B (non-Apostille state): banker's signature notarized, authenticated by the parent country's foreign ministry, legalized by the Korean Embassy/Consulate, and then translated into Korean by a licensed translator. The issuing bank letter must be dated within 30 days of the Korean incorporation application.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, senior managers, and authorized signatories must be screened against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications Lists, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Republic of Korea Designated Individuals under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the FIU Watchlist, as well as the World Bank and ADB debarment lists. Automated continuous screening, adverse-media monitoring, and source-of-funds analysis must be performed at initial onboarding and on a real-time, event-driven basis thereafter; any match above 85% probability score triggers enhanced due diligence, corroborating documentation, and senior compliance officer approval before any capital injection or director appointment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Service (인터넷등기소, i-Ros) at www.iros.go.kr; supplementary National Tax Service HomeTax business name search at www.hometax.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in Korean (Hangul), with an optional English transliteration in parentheses for cross-border recognition. Under Korean Commercial Act Article 17, the trade name must be clearly distinct from existing registered names in the same registry, and it must contain a term denoting the business purpose and must end with the legal form suffix 주식회사 (Chusik Hoesa). Foreign words and brands must be phonetic Hangul transliterations unless the original trademark is internationally well-known and registered; restrictive terms must be approved by the relevant supervising ministry. Four-tier naming conventions are applied: distinct identity token, purpose-relevant token, activity descriptor, and the corporate form suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a name rejection notice from the registry clerk under Article 17-3 of the Commercial Act, the applicant has 14 days to file a written objection and a revised name application with the same District Court Registry Division. If the objection is dismissed, the rejected party may file a petition for correction with the competent High Court under the Registration Act and, in parallel, an administrative lawsuit before the Seoul Administrative Court within 30 days of dismissal notice. Before filing, the applicant must re-run the i-Ros search and obtain a formal name search certificate. The appeal fee is KRW 10,000 (approximately USD 7.50), and the entire correction procedure typically takes 7 to 14 business days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for a hotpot restaurant and condiment supply company under the Food Sanitation Act (Article 15) and the enforcement rules of the National Tax Service. A standard Chusik Hoesa must have a physical place of business (사업장) that serves as the corporate registered address and, for restaurant operations, must include an actual kitchen, dining area, drainage, ventilation, water supply, and waste disposal facilities. The National Tax Service will deny a business registration with a virtual office only for this industry, and banks will reject the current-account application if the corporate address is a mailbox-only premise. A hybrid arrangement where the registered office is a physical leased location separate from or co-located with the restaurant kitchen is acceptable if the address is a real, occupied space, but the corporate registered office must under no circumstances be a virtual mail-forwarding service.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: High (8 out of 10). Check and expect unannounced physical on-site inspections by the municipal district office, public health inspectors under the Food Sanitation Act, and National Tax Service officers. Initial inspections are likely within the first 60 days after obtaining the food business license; thereafter, annual hygiene and VAT serial invoice inspections occur, with supplemental fire safety and labor compliance visits under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. The likelihood increases if customer complaints or anonymous whistle-blower reports are lodged with the local government, or if monthly tax filings show a mismatch between reported sales and POS terminal data. Maintain physically separate counting records, a Korean-language business registration certificate displayed at the premises, and complete condiment inventory labeling to reduce penalty exposure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Trade Name Search and Clearance Certificate via i-Ros
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (i-Ros portal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Certified name search certificate fee under the Korean Court Fees Act; online search itself is free, certificate issuance costs KRW 1,200.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration Duty and Education Surtax on Paid-in Capital of KRW 10,000,000 (Equal to 0.5% Combined)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local Government (Si/Gun/Gu) with collection at the District Court Registry Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration Duty Act, Articles 24 and 26, plus Education Tax Act surtax; computed as 0.4% registration duty plus 0.2% education surtax on subscription capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: District Court Incorporation Registration Fee (Chusik Hoesa Registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court Fees Act Schedule 1 regarding corporate registrations; standard fee KRW 38,000.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate Seal and Seal Certificate Registration (인감신고)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry fee schedule for seal registration and issuance of blank certificate.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Certified Korean Translation of Parent Company Documentary Bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and certified legal translation agency in the Republic of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for notarization of corporate documents and certified Korean translation of approximately 15 to 20 pages.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or Consular Legalization Fees for Five Parent-Company Instruments (Single Applicable Path Only)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the parent jurisdiction or Korean Embassy/Consulate if non-Apostille state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: International apostille and consular fee benchmark at USD 30 per instrument; only one path applies, never both.
Local Fee Ordinance payable upon filing of a food service establishment notification under the Food Sanitation Act.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal Consultation, Drafting of Articles of Association, and Corporate Governance Set-Up
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Korean corporate and commercial law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market flat fee for a Chusik Hoesa incorporation package including articles of incorporation, board resolutions, initial share issuance, and corporate seal handling.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: National Tax Service Business Registration and E-Tax / VAT Registration (홈택스)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official government filing fee; administrative registration is free but legal translation of the registration documents may be required if submitted by a foreign shareholder.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 4470, as amended), Articles 288 to 317 and Articles 375 to 376; Framework Act on Commercial Registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office (Commercial Registration Section) of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office address; in Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registration Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, promoter report, capital deposit certificate, and consent-to-office forms.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Commercial Act. The paid-in capital is the amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation and must be deposited into a bank account opened in the Company name before the incorporation registration application is filed. There is no blocked escrow account requirement; however, the funds must remain on deposit until the registration certificate is issued and the funds can be used only for Company purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The first board of directors of [Entity Name], a Chusik Hoesa organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, acting by unanimous written consent, hereby makes the following resolutions effective immediately after incorporation: FIRST: The Articles of Incorporation prepared by the incorporators are approved in all respects. The form and content of the Articles comply with Article 289 and Article 290 of the Commercial Act, and the directors are directed to file the Articles, together with the required application for registration, with the competent District Court Commercial Registration Office. SECOND: The authorized shares and issued shares of the Company shall be as stated in the Articles. The board approves the subscription of [Number] common shares at a subscription price of [Price] Korean Won per share, resulting in total paid-in capital of [Amount] Korean Won. Each director is authorized to collect the subscription payments, deposit the funds into a bank account opened in the Company name, and deliver proof of deposit to the registration office and National Tax Service. THIRD: The registered office of the Company shall be located at [Address], Republic of Korea. The Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer are jointly authorized to execute and deliver the office use agreement or lease for that address and to file any change of registered office that may later become necessary. FOURTH: The board authorizes the opening of one or more corporate bank accounts at [Bank Name], Korea, and designates [CEO Name] and [CFO Name] as authorized signatories. All withdrawals, agreements, guarantees, and contracts of the Company shall require two authorized signatures unless the board has approved a single signature power for a defined transaction or amount. FIFTH: The following persons are appointed as statutory officers of the Company to serve until the next annual general meeting of shareholders and until their successors are lawfully elected: Chairperson of the Board, [Name]; Representative Director and President, [Name]; Chief Financial Officer, [Name]; and Auditor, [Name]. The Representative Director is designated as the legal representative of the Company. The Auditor shall be independent and shall not serve concurrently as a director or employee of the Company. SIXTH: The directors are authorized to register the Company with the National Tax Service, obtain all tax registrations, corporate seal reporting, and business licenses, obtain the Food Service Business Permit and, if applicable, the Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License required under the Food Sanitation Act, and take any lawful measures necessary for the licensing and operation of the overseas direct-operated hotpot restaurant and condiment supply business, including appointing local counsels, attorneys, and agents in foreign jurisdictions. SEVENTH: The Chairperson, Secretary, or any director is empowered to attest, notarize, apostille, legalize, and deliver all documents required to give full force and effect to these resolutions. This written resolution shall be retained in the corporate records book and shall be binding on all directors, officers, employees, and agents of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Notarize and Fund the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public and the intended corporate bank branch; later pre-filing review by outside corporate counsel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation stating the corporate purpose, authorized capital, issued shares, registered address, paid-in capital, names of directors, statutory auditor, representative director, and fiscal year. Execute the incorporators meeting minutes and have the Articles notarized by a Korean notary as required by the Commercial Act. Open a provisional corporate subscription account at a licensed Korean bank and deposit the full paid-in capital. Conduct AML/KYC checks on each shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner. Have outside counsel review the draft for consistency with the Food Sanitation Act licensing scope and overseas branch plan. Keep the capital deposit certificate ready for submission to the registration office.
required_dossiers: Passports or identification of all shareholders and directors
Power of attorney for any foreign signatory
Registered office use agreement or lease
Consent to office forms for directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or reviewing counsel raises a defect, prepare corrected Articles and re-notarize before filing. If the bank rejects the account opening due to AML/KYC, provide the required beneficial ownership declaration or choose another licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the competent District Court, filed in person or through the Pungseop online registration system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for registration of incorporation of a stock company to the Commercial Registration Section, together with the notarized Articles, capital deposit certificate, proof of registered office, appointment consents, and all statutory forms. Pay the registration tax, education surtax, and court fees. The court registrar will review compliance with the Commercial Act, the legality of the corporate purpose, the identity of directors and auditor, and the validity of capital. If submitted online, upload scanned documents and deliver the original hard copies to the registration office within three business days. After examination the registrar issues the certificate of incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation of a stock company
Proof of registered office lease or address use
Consent to office of each director and auditor
Power of attorney if filing through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for missing documents, file the missing item within the registry correction period. If the registrar finds the Articles defective, submit an amended registration, pay any additional fee, and request expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal, Tax and Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service and the local Si/Gun/Gu tax office; the corporate seal reporting counter is at the tax office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certificate of incorporation registration, report the corporate seal to the local income tax office with jurisdiction over the registered office, then complete the business registration under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Corporate Income Tax Act. The NTS will issue the corporate tax identification number and business license. This registration is required before any commercial transaction. If the Company will conduct food service, the local government food sanitation division should be contacted to start the separate food service business permit process, although that permit is a subsequent licence rather than the general business registration. Also register with the local authorities for electronic tax invoices and for the four major social insurance schemes.
required_dossiers: Corporate seal and corporate seal specimen
Application for corporate registration and tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS or local tax office queries the registration, correct the data and resubmit; if the business license is delayed due to an unverified address, provide the lease certificate or a landlord confirmation and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Food Service and Food Manufacturing Licenses
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety and the local Si/Gun/Gu government with delegated food safety powers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for a Food Service Business Permit for the hotpot restaurant and, if the condiment supply activity includes processing, packing, or manufacturing of food, submit a separate Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License application. Prepare the facility layout, cooking and washing areas, waste disposal contract, and food safety management plans. Passing a hygiene inspection conducted by an MFDS inspector or local government is required. Employee health certificates for kitchen staff, pest control programme, and food allergen labelling documents must be maintained. The permit must be displayed at each facility and kept valid through annual filings.
required_dossiers: Food manufacturing and processing application form (for condiment supply)
Facility floor plan and kitchen layout
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the health inspector denies approval, correct each cited deficiency and request a re-inspection within the statutory period; if the application is rejected administratively, submit an appeal or re-application with a revised HACCP plan.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Fire Safety, Civil Defense, Environmental and Workplace Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Fire Agency, local fire department, Ministry of Environment, and the Ministry of Employment and Labor.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a fire safety certificate under the Act on Firefighting Facilities Installation and Safety Management, covering the building occupancy, fire escapes, extinguishers, gas range, exhaust duct, and any sprinkler system. Submit the building permit and occupancy approval and arrange a fire inspection. For environmental compliance, register the facility or obtain an environmental registration as applicable under the Water Environment Conservation Act, install grease traps and wastewater treatment equipment, and enter into a licensed waste disposal agreement. For workplace safety, file a safety and health plan under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and obtain civil defense clearance for the restaurant occupancy.
required_dossiers: Fire safety certificate application and building certificate
Environmental impact assessment or environmental registration form
Sewer discharge registration or wastewater permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire or environmental approval is refused, remedy any non-conformities and arrange follow-up inspection. For substantive denial, use the administrative appeal process before the relevant agency or the Administrative Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety; local Si/Gun/Gu government with delegated authority; National Fire Agency; Ministry of Environment and Korea Environment Corporation; Ministry of Employment and Labor.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Service Business Permit under the Food Sanitation Act; Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License under the Food Sanitation Act; Fire Safety Certificate; Civil Defense Clearance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, supported by the Korea Environment Corporation and the local environmental protection division.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: For a hotpot restaurant and condiment processing operation, the classification is normally Environmental Registration under the Water Environment Conservation Act if wastewater discharge exceeds the small-scale threshold, or Exempt for a retail-scale restaurant with only sanitary wastewater discharged to public sewer. A Full EIA Report is required only if a project has a gross floor area above 100,000 square meters, is located in an environmentally sensitive zone, or is designated under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to public sewer must meet the effluent standards under the Water Environment Conservation Act: BOD 10 mg/L or less, CODMn 40 mg/L or less, SS 10 mg/L or less, total nitrogen 20 mg/L or less, and total phosphorus 0.2 mg/L or less. Cooking oil and grease must be captured by an interceptor and disposed of by a licensed recycler. Cooking exhaust must be controlled with hoods and scrubbers to satisfy the Odor Prevention Act; VOCs released through ventilation must be controlled if the usage threshold requiring registration is reached. Hazardous waste, including waste acid, solvent, or contaminated food oil, must be handled by a licensed waste disposal contractor and manifested under the Waste Management Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety permit under the Act on Firefighting Facilities Installation and Safety Management, including fire escape routes, extinguishers, gas detection, exhaust duct cleaning, and sprinkler inspection; structural load and occupancy approval from the local building office; civil defense emergency evacuation signage and approval for the restaurant occupancy; and occupational safety and health clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act from the Ministry of Employment and Labor.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr). Customs and export clearance portal: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Chusik Hoesa (Korean stock corporation), the single statutory identifier is the 10-digit Business Registration Number issued by NTS, which serves as Corporate TIN and VAT ID. A foreign non-resident entity entering Korea must first determine if it has a domestic place of business (fixed establishment). If yes, registration is mandatory under the Value-Added Tax Act; if no fixed establishment, the foreign entity should register through a domestic tax representative for any Korean VAT/tax exposure. Procedure: (1) prepare apostilled certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, foreign business license, evidence of Korean place of business (lease or right-to-use agreement), passport/alien registration details of the resident manager, and notarized power of attorney for the tax representative; (2) file the statutory Application for Business Registration with the competent district tax office or via HomeTax; (3) NTS validates the submitted establishment facts and issues the Business Registration Number, generally within three business days; (4) register for electronic tax invoice issuance under HomeTax; (5) if exporting goods, obtain an exporter code from Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS) and register for export declarations. Non-resident entities with no Korean fixed establishment but with Korean-source taxable supplies must nevertheless register, or appoint a Korean tax representative, to file and pay VAT; failure to register exposes the entity to non-deduction of input VAT and penalty surcharges.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea has no check-the-box or pass-through entity election; a Chusik Hoesa is per se taxable as a domestic corporation. Separate statutory elections exist for group tax consolidation of wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries and tax-neutral restructuring (merger/spin-off), but these are not entity-classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover exemption threshold. Every business operator, including foreign entities with a Korean domestic place of business, must register from commencement of taxable business. Simplified taxpayer status applies to small businesses with annual taxable turnover under KRW 80,000,000, but registration remains mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All business-to-business supplies require issuance of an electronic tax invoice through the NTS HomeTax system or an approved e-invoice service provider. The e-tax invoice must be transmitted to NTS no later than the day following the supply date. There is no discretionary VAT pre-clearance approval; anti-fraud control is achieved through mandatory electronic transmission, digitally authenticated issuer credentials, unique sequential invoice numbers, and NTS cross-matching of e-invoices with customs export declarations and corporate VAT returns. Large taxpayers must use system-to-system/API or EDI integrations with HomeTax for bulk transmission. Simplified taxpayers are subject to reduced e-invoicing/cash-receipt obligations, but B2B zero-rated exports must always be supported by a zero-rated electronic tax invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Korean supplier may claim 0% VAT on: (i) tangible goods (e.g., hotpot condiments, packaged food ingredients) physically exported from Korea and cleared by Korea Customs Service under an export declaration; (ii) services supplied to non-residents or to foreign jurisdictions where the place of supply and actual use/benefit are outside Korea, including franchising, management, royalty and offshore digital services; (iii) goods and services supplied for international transportation or overseas construction projects, where statutory evidence exists. For the overseas hotpot dining chain, dining services performed in Korea are standard-rated at 10%; fees charged to overseas franchise affiliates are zero-rated only if the supporting contracts and performance evidence demonstrate actual foreign place of supply/use and foreign currency receipts. Exporters with excess input VAT are entitled to accelerated VAT refunds, subject to production on audit of the full substantive evidence bundle.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service approved Export Declaration (UNI-PASS electronic export clearance, equivalent of customs Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing physical removal from Korea
Overseas sales contract or purchase order
Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / Inward Remittance Certificate and Korean bank certificate showing receipt of foreign currency in Korea
Service performance evidence for qualifying offshore service exports (statement of work, delivery/access logs, overseas user evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS reconciles zero-rated sales against customs export declarations and foreign exchange receipts. If zero-rating is claimed without verified export, or foreign exchange proceeds are not repatriated to Korea within the statutory 180-day period, NTS reverses the zero-rating and assesses 10% VAT on the full supply amount with interest, plus surcharges of up to 20% for negligent under-reporting and up to 40% for intentional concealment or fraudulent false e-tax invoices. Issuing false export tax invoices to obtain zero-rating or input VAT refunds is a criminal tax fraud offence under the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act and may trigger imprisonment/fines, retrospective reassessment within the extended 10-year statute of limitations for offshore fraud, refund clawback, and disqualification of export refund privileges. The taxpayer retains the burden of proof through bills of lading, FIRC, contracts, and service-performance evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as Korea's central bank and foreign exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, operating alongside the Ministry of Economy and Finance's Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized, OECD-compliant foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with current account transactions generally treated as freely convertible while capital account transactions are subject to registration, declaration, and reporting obligations. Non-resident and resident investors may transfer dividends, profits, and liquidation proceeds after tax if the original foreign investment was properly notified to BOK or a designated foreign exchange bank. There are no pervasive rationing rules for ordinary operating receipts; however, the foreign exchange bank remains responsible for verifying the underlying transaction, collecting trade proceeds within statutory deadlines, and reporting settlements through BOK's Foreign Exchange Information System. The main friction for a Korean Chusik Hoesa is not technical inconvertibility but documentary compliance: missing BOK transaction codes, delayed declaration of foreign direct investment, incomplete export or import customs confirmation, or inconsistent beneficiary and reference lines can trigger bank holds and regulatory penalties. Profit remittance to overseas shareholders requires board minutes, audited financial statements, tax withholding documentation if dividends are paid, and a foreign exchange bank remittance declaration. In practice, convertibility is high for lawful operating cash flows, but the compliance burden is asymmetric for cross-border equity injections and overseas disbursements, which require more rigorous underlying documentation and purpose codes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must collect export proceeds through a Korean foreign exchange bank within one year from the export declaration date; extensions may be granted by the foreign exchange bank for justified reasons. There is no mandatory fixed conversion ratio into KRW; export proceeds may be credited to a foreign currency account or converted to KRW at market rates, but every receipt must be reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System and the export declaration must be settled against the actual collection.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Operating Account and Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Direct Investment settlement
Global Trade Corporate Account / Korean Won Operating Account
Enterprise Foreign Exchange Account / Overseas Investment Escrow Account
Trade Plus Multi-Currency Account / Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, foreign exchange business may be conducted only by banks licensed as foreign exchange banks; overseas digital EMIs without a Korean banking license cannot legally maintain corporate KRW or foreign currency operating accounts for a Chusik Hoesa or hold client funds for FX settlement. They may only be used as supplementary payment gateways for local merchant acquiring or POS processing through licensed acquirers, and they must never be treated as the primary treasury, clearing, or FX rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a domestic Chusik Hoesa, at least one statutory representative or a person with express corporate representation authorization must attend the initial account opening in a domestic branch or be verified through a Korean-registered digital onboarding channel permitted by the bank. Non-resident shareholders and directors do not all need to travel if a resident representative presents the corporate seal certificate, articles of incorporation, business registration certificate, and notarized power of attorney; however, many tier-1 banks still require a physical identity interview for the authorized signer and will reject pure remote consular proxy opening unless additional video verification, overseas apostille or consular legalization, and FATCA/CRS self-certifications are completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: KYC ultimate beneficial owner opacity - a Chusik Hoesa with multiple Korean holding layers or foreign nominee shareholders showing no credible source of wealth for an overseas restaurant chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified UBO register with each natural person's copy of passport or national ID, six months of bank statements and source-of-wealth letters, corporate ownership chart, articles of association, board and shareholder minutes approving the ownership structure, foreign investment notification acknowledgements, and any trust or nominee declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business license and operating substance mismatch - the entity's Korean registration shows stock corporation ISIC 5610 dining without a visible Korean storefront, while funds are destined for overseas hotpot operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Overseas direct-operation restaurant agreements or master franchise contracts; lease agreements for the overseas hotpot locations; food service, alcohol, and sanitation licenses in each overseas jurisdiction; local tax registrations; brand and trademark certificates; payroll and management organization charts; and projected profit and loss statements for the overseas dining chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection without matching export or trade rationale - the bank sees remittances from offshore shareholders labeled as investments or loans but cannot map them to Korean-source taxable revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving capital increase or shareholder loan; foreign direct investment declaration acknowledgement; BOK reporting code confirmation; escrow account designation; shareholder loan agreements with repayment schedule; CPA capital verification certificate; and a use-of-funds budget tied to overseas capex or working capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payment fragmentation - repeated low-value wires to seasoning, meat, seafood, or condiment suppliers in high-risk jurisdictions, or to related-party overseas entities, triggering structuring or trade-based laundering checks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreements and source invoices; customs import and export declarations; phytosanitary and food import certificates; trademarked condiment purchase records; genuine end-beneficiary certifications; periodic trade ledger reconciliations; and bank reference letters from the counterparty banks.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank as the receiving bank. The overseas shareholder must wire via SWIFT MT103 to the entity's Capital Escrow Account or operating account with the precise shareholder name, investment reference, and appropriate BOK foreign exchange purpose code. For foreign direct investment, ensure prior foreign investment notification or declaration is filed through KOTRA or the designated bank; after receipt, the bank will report settlement through BOK's Foreign Exchange Information System. For a shareholder loan, register the loan with the foreign exchange bank and retain the loan agreement, interest terms, and board resolution. If the inbound remittance funds an overseas branch or restaurant subsidiary, it should be classified as an overseas direct investment or foreign business establishment filing rather than ordinary trading receipts; CPA capital verification is recommended before converting funds into KRW.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to overseas suppliers and related restaurant entities, use domestic Korean banks with standard SWIFT MT103 direct remittances for T/T payments; for contract-heavy transactions, issue commercial letters of credit at sight or usance, or use documentary collection through the supplier's bank. Each remittance must be supported by the import declaration where relevant, underlying commercial invoices, contracts, and an approved BOK transaction code. For ongoing overseas branch and restaurant expenses, use an overseas direct investment annual reporting mechanism and remit through the designated foreign exchange bank, avoiding split payments and maintaining a complete audit trail for the clearing of trade and non-trade disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with maturity up to twelve months covering committed trade receivables and payables in KRW, USD, and other widely traded currencies
Non-deliverable forwards executed with licensed Korean banks for currencies without organized deliverable liquidity, subject to substantive underlying trade exposure and BOK reporting requirements

Cross-currency swaps permitted only for documented funding, overseas investment, or asset-liability matching purposes, with foreign exchange bank registration and no speculative net open position build-up

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Local Income Tax Surtax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and the competent local government tax office (Seoul/regional Metropolitan City or Province)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the 3rd month following the fiscal year end (for a December 31 fiscal year, by March 31 of the following year); request for preliminary return by last day of the 2nd month is also common for corporations with large business sites
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts an administrative penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax, plus annual interest at 0.022% per day; understatement penalty of 10% of the under-reported amount or 20% for foreign transaction items; continued non-payment triggers asset seizure under the National Tax Collection Act and, if the company remains dormant for 3 consecutive years without tax filings, administrative dissolution and strike-off from the Korean Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report on Financial Statements (if statutory thresholds are met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the company's own shareholders at the ordinary general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ordinary general meeting of shareholders must be held within 3 months of fiscal year end; the external audit report must be tabled there and the final audit report must be delivered to the FSS within 2 weeks after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a mandatory external audit results in a prohibition on the company's financial statements being approved, administrative fines of up to KRW 50 million (approximately USD 38,000) on the company and its directors, and may lead to a court-ordered audit; in severe cases of accounting fraud, criminal liability includes imprisonment up to 7 years and additional fines, and the company may be suspended or dissolved administratively.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report on Overseas Direct Investment (Outward FDI) covering overseas restaurant subsidiaries or branches
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bank of Korea (submitted through a designated domestic foreign exchange bank) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By February 28 of the year following the reporting calendar year; changes in overseas investment value, shareholding, or operation status must also be reported within 30 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file an overseas direct investment report is subject to a fine of up to KRW 10 million (approximately USD 7,600); providing false information may lead to imprisonment for up to 3 years or a fine, and repeated non-compliance may cause the Bank of Korea to impose administrative sanctions on the company and its audit firm.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registration of Director and Auditor Changes Following the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Department of the District Court where the company's registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days from the date of the annual general meeting if directors or auditors are re-elected or changed; also within 14 days for any change in representative director
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of commercial registration changes attracts a court penalty or administrative fine; continuous failure to reflect the current directors in the commercial register can impair the company's legal capacity to bind itself, expose the company to claims of good-faith third parties against unauthorized representatives, and ultimately lead to the court ordering a judicial correction or strike-off for non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent external audit is mandatory for a Chusik Hoesa if: (a) total assets at the end of the relevant fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.1 million); (b) the company is a listed or otherwise publicly traded company regardless of asset size; (c) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion and total liabilities equal or exceed KRW 7 billion (balance-sheet insolvency indicators) or the company has issued debentures to the public; or (d) the Financial Services Commission or the Securities and Futures Commission designates the company for audit-based reasons of public interest or creditor protection. For companies falling below these triggers, no mandatory external audit is required, but management must still prepare tax-adjustment financial statements and may voluntarily engage a registered CPA for certification.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, the Korean adoption of IFRS) is mandatory for listed companies and companies subject to external audit of a public-interest scale; non-public companies may use Korean GAAP (General Corporate Accounting Standards, K-GAAP) or the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small and Medium Enterprises; in all cases, required statutory books and financial statements must be prepared annually under the Korean Commercial Act and the External Audit Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not impose an annual beneficial-owner confirmation return, but a Chusik Hoesa must maintain an up-to-date register of shareholders and any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be reflected without delay. Statutory reporting obligations include: (i) any change in directors, representative director, or auditor must be registered with the District Court within 14 days; (ii) a foreign investor or a Korean company holding overseas investment must report material changes to the Bank of Korea within 30 days; and (iii) for tax purposes, any change in controlling shareholders or beneficial owners must be disclosed in the annual corporate income tax return by March 31. Failure to maintain an accurate shareholder register may invalidate the company's dividend payments and share rights vis-à-vis bona fide third parties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Auditors and/or Audit Committee Members (if appointed)
Minute Book of Shareholders' General Meetings
Minute Book of Board of Directors' Meetings
Commercial Books and Accounting Records (장부 및 재무기록)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – 1,500 (KRW 650,000 – 1,950,000) per year for registered office, statutory agent, and commercial registry compliance support in a major jurisdiction such as Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – 25,000 (KRW 10,000,000 – 32,500,000) per year if a statutory certified CPA audit is required, depending on asset size, number of overseas branches, and complexity of the hotpot restaurant chain and condiment supply operations

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.4% combined top marginal corporate income tax rate (24% national CIT plus 10% local income tax surtax, i.e., 24% + 2.4%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption for qualifying foreign dividends (100% exemption where the Korean parent holds at least 10% of the overseas subsidiary and the subsidiary meets genuine business substance requirements); foreign tax credit for foreign taxable income; R&D tax credit up to 30% of qualifying R&D spending; facility investment tax credit (10% for eligible capital investments); potential tax holidays in Free Economic Zones for qualifying foreign-invested businesses. For overseas branch income, direct foreign tax credit eliminates double taxation, rendering the effective rate on host-country taxed income equal to the difference between the host rate and the Korean combined rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for Domestic Corporation (Form 17-S-4 'Corporate Income Tax Return') and its attached schedules, filed electronically via the National Tax Service HomeTax System (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year (e.g., by March 31 for a calendar-year taxpayer). When the corporate accounts are certified by a licensed tax accountant or auditor, an extension of up to 45 days is granted upon application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal Year (Business Year) – start date and end date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact global fiscal year. If a foreign branch uses a different annual accounting period, align the foreign branch's audited results to the parent Korean fiscal year end using exchange rates published by the Bank of Korea. For non-resident shareholders, this Box determines the attribution of distributions and the applicable domestic and treaty withholding timing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate Identification, Taxpayer Number, and Shareholder Information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide company name, corporate registration number, head office address, and representative director identity. Disclose all non-resident shareholders holding 5% or more of the issued shares, their jurisdiction of residence, and their tax identification numbers. This data drives the withholdings for non-resident dividends and any treaty rate claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of Total Income and Deductions (Profit or Loss Reconciliation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter entire worldwide gross revenue, including overseas hotpot restaurant turnovers, franchise fees, condiment supply revenue, and royalties from intellectual property. Include all foreign branch revenue converted to KRW at the Bank of Korea final base rate of the fiscal year-end. Add back non-deductible items such as excess entertainment expenses, excessive director remuneration, and corporate income tax paid. Ensure that foreign taxes are only claimed as credit, not deducted, to avoid double counting.

Carry forward domestic qualifying losses up to 10 years. Apply participation exemptions, R&D deductions, and other tax incentives. For non-resident source income, first deduct foreign-source expenses (allocable overheads, foreign branch marketing costs, support staff expenses) to compute net foreign-source taxable income. The NTS may require a jurisdictional breakdown of foreign income and local taxes paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate Income Tax, Local Income Tax, and Progressivity Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply progressive national corporate income tax rates (9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% up to KRW 20 billion; 21% up to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion) to the taxable base. Compute the 10% local income tax surtax on the national tax amount. Foreign branch profits from overseas restaurants are included in the base, so the resulting total tax is subject to the foreign tax credit in Box 6.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign Tax Credit and Treaty Application Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a detailed jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction schedule of foreign corporate income taxes paid by and on behalf of the Korean entity on foreign-source income. Claim a direct foreign tax credit limited to the Korean corporate tax attributable to that foreign-source income. If a Double Tax Agreement (DTA) with the host country provides for an exemption instead of credit, attach the relevant Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) of the Korean company and the treaty provision relied upon. Treat tax sparing credits, if any, in accordance with the DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-Resident Shareholder and Consultant Withholding Summary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all dividends, interest, and royalties remitted to non-residents during the fiscal year. Enter the statutory withholding rates and the treaty-reduced rates. For royalty payments to a foreign licensor, state whether beneficial ownership and economic substance conditions are satisfied; obtain and attach the foreign TRC and a statement of actual business activity in the foreign jurisdiction. Interest paid to non-residents under a back-to-back loan arrangement may require a beneficial ownership declaration and anti-treaty-shopping disclosures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attachments: Financial Statements, Auditor Certification, and Supplementary Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (KIFRS) or K-GAAP financial statements, tax reconciliation statements, and the independent accountant's audit report (if applicable). Add the foreign branch financial statements and local host-country tax returns. Non-resident related party transactions over the applicable threshold must be disclosed in Form No. 17 'Foreign Related Party Transaction Statement'.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-reporting triggers a proportional penalty: 20% of the unpaid corporate tax for unfaithful under-reporting, increased to 40% if the under-reporting is fraudulent; failure to report the tax base by the statutory deadline without a justifiable cause also incurs an additional 20%. If the taxpayer merely files late and pays after the deadline, late payment surcharge accrues at 0.025% per day on the unpaid amount until fully paid. Submission of a grossly false return with intent to evade may be prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with maximum imprisonment of 2 years (5 years when the tax evaded exceeds KRW 500 million) and fines. In addition, unfaithful foreign transaction reporting can invoke penalties under the Act on Coordination of International Tax Affairs, including a 10% adjustment penalty and a KRW 2 million fine for non-submission of the Foreign Related Party Transaction Statement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% effective statutory dividend withholding tax: 20% national dividend withholding tax under Article 156(1) of the Income Tax Act, plus 10% local income tax surtax (2%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty-reduced dividend withholding (typically 5% for 10%+ corporate shareholders, or 10-15% for portfolio investors), the Korean payor must obtain from the non-resident beneficiary before the payment date: (i) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the beneficiary's competent authority for the fiscal year of distribution, (ii) an executed Form of 'Beneficial Ownership and DTA Application' with the NTS, and (iii) evidence that the beneficial owner is not merely a shell or flow-through entity, including substance documentation (employees, premises, and actual operational risk). The application form must be filed with the district tax office before the distribution remittance; if the application is rejected, the statutory 22% must be withheld and deposited. Where treaty relief is only identified after the payment, a refund claim or correction scope can be filed within 3 years from the statutory due date of the tax, with interest and no penalty if the refund is granted. For dividends flowing to a foreign parent headquartered in a jurisdiction participating in the OECD MLI, the Principal Purpose Test also requires a genuine business purpose for the entity holding the Korean shares.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and interest from a Korean payor to a non-resident is 22% (20% national tax + 2% local income tax surcharge). Applicable Double Tax Agreements generally reduce interest withholding to 10% (e.g., Korea-US) or 0% in some cases for government/qualified institutions, and reduce royalty withholding to 10% or 15% depending on treaty. The reduction is available only upon the same TRC and beneficial ownership process, and for royalties, the recipient must prove that the intellectual property is genuinely developed and managed in its own jurisdiction and that no bare licensing arrangement exists. Royalties paid to a non-resident for the use of restaurant trademarks or culinary recipes are subject to the withholding at the payment date, whether or not the payment is in domestic or foreign currency, and the non-resident licensee must file a domestic income tax return through its fiscal agent if the withholding is not fully settled.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 500 million aggregate foreign-related party transactions in a fiscal year triggers mandatory filing of the Foreign Related Party Transaction Statement with the annual corporate tax return. Local File (and Master File if applicable) is mandatory when foreign-related party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion in a year and the total revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion; however, to avoid NTS audit risk, contemporaneous documentation is recommended for any intercompany transaction regardless of threshold, especially for trademark royalty flows and condiment supply agreements.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies a strong substance-over-form and anti-avoidance framework: under Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, transactions structured to artificially avoid tax will be recharacterized. For foreign subsidiaries and branches, the Korean Controlled Foreign Company (CFC) rules attribute undistributed foreign income to the Korean parent when the foreign entity lacks genuine economic activities. The Korean-foreign hotpot chain must demonstrate that each overseas unit has substantial operational management, staffing, physical premises, and real decision-making for menu development, local licensing, and quality control. A purely paper arrangement with a foreign holding company claiming treaty benefits will be denied under the OECD Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test, and the NTS will reclassify the royalty or dividend as domestic-source income, triggering 22% withholding and subject to additional civil penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Under-Reporting of Overseas Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating overseas hotpot restaurants through unreported cash registers, omitting foreign branch gross receipts from the Korean corporate income tax return, and falsifying profit and loss statements to understate taxable income. This includes using nominal contracts with local store managers to hide profits and failing to record foreign bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 9(1), evasion by fraud or willful misrepresentation is punishable with imprisonment for up to 2 years, or a fine not exceeding 2 times the evaded tax. If the evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million, imprisonment may extend to 5 years. The National Tax Service also imposes an additional 40% fraudulent return penalty plus late payment surcharge at 0.025% per day on the entire under-reported amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed false returns or directed the concealment are personally liable for the evaded tax and penalties under the secondary liability rule (Framework Act on National Taxes Art. 39). The NTS may seize personal bank accounts, impose a travel ban (blacklisting as repeating tax evader), and refer the case to the prosecutor, leading to criminal conviction, incarceration, and disbarment from serving as a corporate officer.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Non-Resident Dividend/Royalty Tax & Improper Treaty Application
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean company pays dividends to a foreign shareholder, or royalties to a non-resident licensor, without withholding the 22% statutory tax, and files a treaty-based exemption without possessing a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) or without proving beneficial ownership. This includes executing sham cost-sharing agreements or interposing a shell entity in a treaty jurisdiction solely to reduce the withholding rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The corporate payor becomes jointly and severally liable for the unpaid withholding tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act plus an additional 20% (40% if intentional) under the Framework Act Art. 47-2, and a 0.025% daily late payment surcharge. If the payor intentionally omits withholding, the director may face criminal sanctions under Article 12 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to 2 years. The dishonest treaty relief claim can be voided ab initio, and the entire 22% plus penalties becomes immediately collectible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed for the deficiency, penalties, and surcharges when the company cannot pay. The NTS will pierce the corporate veil and hold each responsible director jointly and severally liable. In serious cases, the tax authority will file a criminal complaint for tax evasion; the director may be extradited or subject to an Interpol Red Notice if already abroad, and any personal assets (including foreign shares, bank accounts, and real estate) are subject to seizure and auction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation & False Related-Party Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Chusik Hoesa sells hotpot condiments and equipment to its foreign subsidiary or branch at a non-arm's length price to shift taxable profits to a lower-tax jurisdiction. It deliberately omits the intercompany transaction schedule from the tax return, does not prepare contemporaneous TP documentation, and signs a master file claiming no transactions with related parties when actual foreign-related transactions exceed the KRW 500 million threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Act on Coordination of International Tax Affairs Art. 5 and Corporate Income Tax Act Art. 76-5-3, the NTS will reassess taxable income at the arm's length price and impose an adjustment penalty of 10% of the adjusted income amount. If the statement of foreign transactions is not submitted or is falsely submitted, an additional KRW 2 million penalty applies. Intentional manipulation with deliberate false documentation constitutes tax evasion under Article 9 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, punishable by imprisonment up to 2 years (or 5 years if evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the false statement or who established a haphazard transfer pricing policy are personally liable for the reassessed tax, adjustment penalty, and daily surcharges when the corporate entity is asset-drained. More critically, individual directors can be subjected to a 'personal asset preservation order' by the NTS, seizure of shares and property, and an exit ban preventing them from leaving Korea until the assessed amount is secured. Criminal referral may lead to a prison sentence; if the director is a foreign national, the Korean court may impose a fine and the director may be barred from re-entering Korea.
